jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado & DOJ Civil Division

headline: Senior-Care Operator InnovAge Pays $36 Million to Settle First-of-Its-Kind Medicare PACE False Claims Case
deck: Federal prosecutors accused the Denver company of collecting monthly capitated payments while delaying cardiology, neurology, and oncology referrals. InnovAge admitted no liability and no executives were charged.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: $36M civil False Claims Act settlement ($25.7M federal, $10.3M states) with no admission of liability and zero individual charges or custody.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Billing Medicaid $22,000 for home-health visits that were never delivered
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: 12–24 months prison plus mandatory federal healthcare program exclusion

sources.title: PACE Organization InnovAge Agrees to Pay $36M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations of Failing to Provide Necessary Medical Care to Seniors

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington. The Civil Division called the $36 million InnovAge agreement its first False Claims Act settlement with a PACE operator.
